title: Microrelease safety narrative and testbed notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a narrative-driven safety playbook and lightweight testbed plan for microreleases (sub-5% exposure canaries, rapid A/B splits) of LLM features routed via Redwood Console. It's intentionally pragmatic: a short checklist + signal map + experiment scaffolding we can use for fast iteration while minimizing operational blast radius.

Context / why this doc exists:
- We've been doing larger phased canaries that take days to ramp. For small feature changes (prompt template tweak, reranker weighting, decoder param change) we want a faster rhythm (hours) with automated safe-guards.
- Ops complexity comes from three tension points: (1) telemetry blindspots for emergent failure modes, (2) noisy metrics when slices are small, (3) unclear human-responsibility at failure thresholds. This doc focuses on concrete mitigation patterns.

Scope (what counts as a microrelease):
- Change surface limited to model serving path: prompt/response post-processing, reranker weight, fallback model variant, short-lived prompt hooks.
- Exposure: 0.1%–5% of traffic for 1–8 hours with rapid rollback paths.
- Not in scope: infra changes, GPU driver updates, major model version swaps (those follow full canary playbooks).

Safety narrative (high level story to communicate to stakeholders):
- "Small change, measured mirror": Spin up a shadow mirror route with the new change receiving mirrored requests (no customer impact), run validations for 30–60 minutes before opening traffic. If mirror validates, open a tiny live cohort (0.1–0.5%) and watch diagnostics for 30 minutes. If stable, double exposure every 20–30 minutes until reaching target. Always keep an escape hatch to immediately switch traffic back to baseline variant.

Minimum telemetry / signal map (startup checklist):
- SLO & availability: 95p latency for requests in the slice vs baseline (compare tail latency).
- Correctness proxies: task-specific evaluation metric(s) (e.g., rerank NDCG@10, hallucination heuristics rate, toxicity score).
- Customer impact proxies: failed calls / 4xx/5xx rate, user-visible error rate, fallback-to-baseline fraction.
- Cost & capacity: token-per-request delta, GPU utilization on pods serving the slice.
- Behavioral drift heuristics: distribution of response lengths, repetition score, unique token entropy.
- Alerting policy: create ephemeral alerts for the slice scoped to 15–30 minute windows with higher sensitivity than prod (e.g., 1.5x usual threshold).

Experiment configuration template (fields to fill for each microrelease):
- experiment_id: brief-id (e.g., micro-rr-202503)
- owner: name + primary oncall (ops)
- change_summary: 1-2 sentence description of what is changing
- mirror_validation_checks: list of mirror checks (synthetic prompt set pass rate, no increase in hallucination tokens)
- initial_exposure: 0.1%–0.5%
- max_exposure: target percent (<=5%)
- exposure_ramp: doubling schedule (minutes between steps)
- min_watch_window: 30 minutes at each step (shorter only with exec signoff)
- rollback_criteria: explicit thresholds per signal (e.g., any of: latency > 2x baseline p95 for 10m, error rate increase > 0.5pp absolute, NDCG drop > 2 points)
- automated_actions: e.g., auto-cut traffic to 0% or switch to variant B, notify channels
- postmortem_window: retain logs and telemetry for 30 days, summary within 72 hours if rollback triggered

Testbed checklist (pre-release):
- unit + integration: changed component covered by CI (yes/no)
- synthetic-bench: run 1k synthetic requests through mirror route, compare to baseline metric vector
- eval-set-run: run existing prompt testset and check N metrics (preapproved)
- dependency-check: confirm model variant compatibility and tokenization parity
- capacity-check: ensure pods have headroom for spikes (CPU/GPU margin > 15%)
- cost-estimate: token delta per hour at planned exposure (quick calc)
- comms: brief on-call and product steward, post experiment in #release-ops with experiment_id

Fast ops recipes (what to do when things look bad):
- noisy spike / transient blip: expand watch window to 60m, keep exposure constant, add extra synthetic probes (run every 5m)
- consistent degradation in correctness proxy: immediately cut exposure 90% and increase mirror traffic to validate fix in isolation
- latency tail growth: revert to baseline routing gradually and trigger auto-rollback if >2x p95 persists for 10m
- user-visible errors: immediate 0% cut, pager escalation to oncall, create incident doc and postmortem owner

Rollout runbook (quick steps for operator):
1) Create experiment in Console with experiment_id, mirror route enabled.
2) Run mirror validation for 30m and collect synthetic probe results.
3) Open exposure to initial_exposure (0.1%–0.5%). Start ephemeral alerts and noise filters.
4) After min_watch_window (30m) and green signals, ramp per exposure_ramp.
5) If any rollback_criteria hit, trigger automated rollback (Console action) and notify stakeholders.
6) After reaching max_exposure and stable for 2x watch windows, mark experiment as stable and schedule postmortem notes and metrics snapshot.

Lightweight postmortem template (if rollback or anomaly):
- brief: what did we change and when
- timeline: mirror -> open -> ramp -> anomaly -> rollback
- signals: which metrics deviated, with delta and windows
- root cause hypothesis + immediate fix
- mitigation to prevent recurrence (monitoring, canary step changes, automation)
- owner for follow-ups and ETA

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve in governance doc:
- Sensitivity vs noise: what aggregate minimum sample size do we require to trust a correctness proxy at 0.5% exposure? (statistical power guidance needed)
- Automation aggressiveness: when is auto-rollback acceptable vs requiring human-in-loop? (default: auto for infrastructural failures, manual for quality regressions)
- Canary duration: can we safely shorten watch windows for iterative product teams? propose split: infra vs quality microreleases.

Action items (next steps):
- Maya: draft a short Confluence page mapping this narrative to existing Console controls (due 2025-03-10) (CONF-12345)
- Ibrahim: implement ephemeral alert templates and CLI commands to spin experiment with default guardrails (JIRA-8271) due 2025-03-14
- Samir: build the synthetic probe set and add to the mirror-runner harness (PR referenced above)
- Claire: run two pilot microreleases this sprint with product teams (search rerank, summarization prompt tweak) and capture results

Quick reference commands / links:
- github PR for harness: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/42
- temporary alert template in PagerDuty: PD-template-microrelease-v1
- Slack channel for ops: #release-ops (thread pinned: microrelease-runbook)

Notes-to-self / rough thoughts (informal):
- We should default mirrors to 1% of mirrored traffic for better stats if the downstream cost is acceptable.
- Consider a lightweight A/B analysis harness that pools runtime microreleases across weeks to build better power estimates for low-exposure experiments.
- If we see repeated microrelease rollbacks on the same feature, escalate to a full canary with longer ramp + human signoff.

References:
- existing canary playbooks in same folder (see rollout-runway-and-stoplight-framework-wip.json)
- internal convos: slack thread 2025-02-14 #release-ops

End of note.

-- Claire NG
